thresholdCalibration.method: For each window, take the maximum standardized statistic across 41 measured variables; use nearest-rank rank 49 (conformal-style calibration).

thresholds.statistic: residual standard-deviation ratio after linear detrending

phase_partition.intermediate: all windows between initial and late phases

global_persistence.policy: do not infer from a two-window episode alone; always report active fraction, sign consistency, and late-regime activity
global_persistence.strict_level_label: active in every window, one sign throughout, and active in the late regime
global_persistence.strict_drift_label: slope active in every window with one sign, window means evolving coherently in that direction, and active in the late regime
global_persistence.strict_variability_label: active in every window and active in the late regime

temporalRules.transient: dynamic feature active initially, lower later, and inactive in the late regime while a possible level displacement can remain

featureSemantics.shift_sigma: signed displacement of the window mean in baseline standard-deviation units
featureSemantics.slope_sigma_h: signed local OLS trend in baseline standard deviations per hour
featureSemantics.residual_std_ratio: ratio of residual standard deviations after linear detrending
featureSemantics.diff_std_ratio: ratio of standard deviations of first differences; sample-to-sample variation
featureSemantics.raw_std_ratio: descriptive ratio of raw standard deviations; overall dispersion only

verbalizationRules.reporting: For each window, name the leading variable (largest above-threshold magnitude) for each statistic, or report none; include the leading rapid-variability variable when present and the largest overall dispersion ratio.
verbalizationRules.overallDispersion: Descriptive standard-deviation ratio; not thresholded as a fault feature.
